clue.text: In favour of cast showing great insight

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A theatre company praised for a production full of deep understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep thinking that shows great insight is called profound, a synonym.

clue.text: Note the procedure for going to get help

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a course of action is a procedure

explanation.surface: Someone notes the steps to follow when seeking assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recourse means turning to a source of aid when in difficulty.

clue.text: Brewed stingo fit for New Year celebration

indicators.note: brewing turns ingredients into something new, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Strong ale brewed fit for seeing in the New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: Stingo is an old word for strong beer, a fine decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England the first visitor of the year brings luck, a Hogmanay custom.

clue.text: Duke left town in a state of flux

indicators.note: the duke has left, so his letter goes

parts.note: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London

explanation.surface: A duke departs a town that is in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsteady and changing is shaky, in a state of flux.

clue.text: Driver, little woman covered in ointment, overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole is turned upside down, read bottom to top
the little woman is wrapped inside the ointment

parts.note: nard, or spikenard, is an aromatic ointment
Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A driver overturns, with a small woman smeared in balm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overturned' reads the whole block bottom to top; 'covered in' means smeared inside the balm. Amy is the youngest March sister in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A drayman drove a dray, a brewer's cart, so he is a driver.

clue.text: Severely punished boy for embracing girl

indicators.note: the boy's letters hug the girl's

parts.note: a lad is a boy
she stands for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A boy is beaten for cuddling a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipped hard, as with a lash, is severely punished.

clue.text: It is about to become an educational establishment

indicators.note: the SA letters go round the other word

parts.note: it is a coy term for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: Something is about to turn into a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal is a crossword convention. 'become an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoa was the porch in Athens where Zeno taught, so the Stoic school itself.

clue.text: View crop pest ravaged

indicators.note: ravaged things are wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Looking over a field where a pest has damaged the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide outlook or scene is a view, a synonym.

clue.text: Star rode around recklessly in … a vehicle

indicators.note: letters thrown about recklessly are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity drives dangerously in a car, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 10 across: its definition, 'a vehicle', is printed at the start of the next clue, which uses the same words again for its own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An open two-seater sports car is a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: : a vehicle, following double bend to arrive at rocky mountain-side

indicators.note: the car comes after the bend, so its letters follow

parts.note: the letter S has the shape of a double bend in a road
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car rounds an S-bend and reaches a craggy slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 9 across; 'a vehicle' serves as that clue's definition and as this clue's CAR. 'to arrive at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep rocky face on a hillside is a scar, mainly a northern English term.

clue.text: Say he's better-developed, and sow dissension

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a man's fuller growth and stirs up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: a cereal plant is set, or well formed, by its ears of grain, so a plant better developed is set by the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: To set people by the ears is an idiom for making them quarrel; read literally, grain crops develop by putting out ears.

clue.text: Exam once over, a defender who'll wriggle out of anything?

indicators.note: the letters are turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: the CSE, Certificate of Secondary Education, was a former British school exam
an apologist defends a cause

explanation.surface: With the test finished, an advocate who always finds a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' signals the CSE is no longer taken; it was replaced in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape artist like Houdini can free himself from any restraint.

clue.text: Judge taking a lead outside building

indicators.note: the lead letters sit on the outside, enclosing the rest

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a ref, short for referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: A judge escorts someone out of a building, holding a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a leash or a front position, but it is the metal; 'taking' is a link and 'outside' wraps the metal round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory-made house put up quickly on site is a kind of building.

clue.text: Jack, Diana and Kathleen, say, to step down

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor
Di is the short form of Diana
Cate is a pet form of Catherine, of which Kathleen is the Irish version

explanation.surface: A list of three people named, as examples, who resign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the names as examples of forms to be shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a throne or office is to resign, which is to step down.

clue.text: Rally soldiers going to the front

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
a front is a cover, a respectable face hiding something

explanation.surface: Soldiers are rallied as they head off to the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' suggests a battle line, but it means a cover, as for a criminal business. 'going to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally after illness or a setback is to get better, a synonym.

clue.text: Naomi was not so hard-hearted

explanation.surface: The biblical Naomi was not a cruel woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi's daughter-in-law Ruth refused to leave her, so Naomi was never without Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiless is hard-hearted; and Naomi, with Ruth always beside her, was never lacking that companion.

clue.text: Business in a stronger position assigned two lines

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
being up means ahead or winning
let means rented or allotted, as a let property

explanation.surface: A firm on the up is given two lines of credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of rhyming verse lines makes a short stanza of that name.

clue.text: Directly I got hurt, treatment was provided

indicators.note: treatment works on something, here reworking the letters

explanation.surface: As soon as someone was injured, they were looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight away and without reserve both fit; directly and plainly are synonyms.

clue.text: English girl, one performing in broadcast

parts.note: a miss is a girl
I is the Roman numeral one
on stage, a performer is on

explanation.surface: An English girl is acting in a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmission sent out over radio or television is a broadcast.

clue.text: Mangle's double, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a ringer is a lookalike, a double

explanation.surface: A clothes mangle's lookalike, judging by its noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An old laundry mangle squeezed water out of washing between rollers.

clue.text: Cops and robbers film — time invested in the shoot

indicators.note: put inside, as money is invested in a venture

parts.note: a tiller is a shoot that springs from the base of a plant
hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A police film with a gunfight, the time spent on shooting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests filming or gunfire; it is a plant's side growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime story full of suspense is the kind of movie called a thriller.

clue.text: Landlord's communication

explanation.surface: A message from the owner of a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord lets out rooms, so is one who lets; and a written message is a communication.

clue.text: Story about "The King and I made into a film

indicators.note: the story goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tale is a story
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A story about the musical The King and I being turned into a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made into a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An early motion picture with a soundtrack was called a talkie.

clue.text: Established the yen without resistance

indicators.note: here in its old sense of outside, wrapping round

parts.note: a yen is a longing
to make a stand is to resist

explanation.surface: The Japanese currency, unopposed, is now firmly set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' points at Japanese money, but it is a strong desire; 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has existed for a long time is established, a synonym.

clue.text: By a quarter? Earnings cut by 5/8

parts.note: north, N, is one of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: five of the word's eight letters are cut away, leaving three

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether pay was cut by a quarter, when it fell by five eighths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' suggests a fraction, matching the surface arithmetic; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Near as a preposition means close by.

clue.text: Incomplete national flag

indicators.note: the word is left unfinished, losing its final letter

parts.note: an Irish citizen is a national of Ireland

explanation.surface: A country's banner left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' suggests a banner; it is the plant called yellow flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, so flag names that plant.

clue.text: Put one's foot down, and start to effect large-scale movement

parts.note: someone who stamped put a foot down hard

indicators.note: the start of the word effect supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone takes a firm line and begins a sweeping change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' looks like insisting; it is literal stamping.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rush of panicking animals or people is a mass movement.

clue.text: Going off round a turning

indicators.note: the rotting letters go round the A

parts.note: food going off is rotting

explanation.surface: Something spoils as it goes round a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning about an axis is turning, a synonym.
